The lighting system includes multiple illumination sources arranged to render a lighting scene within an environment occupied by a user. These illumination sources may be positioned at different places in the environment and may cooperate to create a desired visual effect, ambience, or functional lighting condition.

Each illumination source is provided with a location sensor configured to detect the position of that illumination source relative to at least one reference point. This reference point is defined independently of the lighting scene, meaning that it does not depend on the particular lighting effect being rendered. Instead, it may correspond to a fixed point in the environment, a user-defined point, a structural feature, or another reference used to establish a spatial relationship between the illumination sources and the environment.

At least one of the illumination sources also includes an additional sensor for detecting further characteristics of the source. For example, the illumination source may include an orientation sensor configured to determine the direction in which the source is aimed or facing. Alternatively, or additionally, the illumination source may include a luminaire type sensor configured to identify the type of luminaire being used, such as a spotlight, floodlight, wall washer, pendant light, or other lighting device. This information allows the system to understand not only where a source is located, but also how it is capable of contributing to the overall lighting scene.

A controller is communicatively coupled to the illumination sources and is configured to send control signals to them. These control signals determine how the illumination sources operate, including parameters such as intensity, color, beam direction, timing, distribution, or other lighting characteristics. Through these commands, the controller coordinates the illumination sources so that they collectively render the intended lighting scene in the environment.

The controller further determines the intended location of an illumination effect within the environment. Based on the detected locations of the illumination sources, and where available their detected orientation or luminaire type, the controller adapts the control commands sent to the illumination sources. By doing so, the controller ensures that the lighting scene is rendered relative to the defined reference point rather than merely according to fixed output settings. This enables the system to compensate for changes in source placement, orientation, or luminaire configuration, thereby producing a lighting scene that remains spatially consistent and appropriate for the user’s environment.
outputs.L4:
A lighting system includes a plurality of illumination sources, such as lamps, luminaires, light modules, or other controllable light-emitting devices, arranged to produce a desired lighting scene within an environment. Each illumination source is associated with one or more sensors or sensing arrangements capable of determining information about that source. The sensed information includes at least the position or location of each illumination source within the environment. For at least one of the illumination sources, the sensed information further includes an orientation of the source, such as the direction in which it is aimed, or information identifying the type of luminaire being used, such as whether the source is a spotlight, wash light, wall washer, directional fixture, diffuse fixture, or another type of lighting device.

The lighting system also includes a controller configured to receive the information obtained from the sensors and to use that information when generating or modifying control commands for the illumination sources. Rather than defining a lighting scene only in terms of fixed commands for fixed lamp positions, the controller defines or interprets the scene relative to an independently specified point, reference location, coordinate system, object, person, or region within the environment. This reference may be independent of the actual positions of the illumination sources, allowing the desired lighting effect to be described in terms of where it should appear or what it should illuminate, rather than in terms of which source should emit which light level or beam direction.

Using the detected position information, and where available the detected orientation or luminaire-type information, the controller determines where light emitted by each illumination source is expected to fall. The controller may calculate, estimate, or otherwise determine the location at which a particular illumination effect will occur, such as a highlighted area, a beam spot, a colored region, a shadowed region, a wall-washing effect, or an illumination pattern. The controller can then compare the expected effect location with the intended location of the lighting scene and adapt the operating commands sent to the illumination sources accordingly.

For example, if a directional luminaire has been moved, rotated, replaced with a different type of fixture, or otherwise altered, the controller can compensate by adjusting parameters such as intensity, color, beam angle, focus, aiming direction, distribution, or the selection of which sources contribute to a given effect. If one illumination source can no longer produce the intended effect because of its new position or orientation, the controller may modify its command, reduce its contribution, or assign all or part of the effect to another source better suited to produce it. Similarly, when a luminaire type is identified, the controller may account for the expected light distribution of that type when determining how to render the scene.

As a result, the desired lighting scene can be reproduced more accurately even when the physical arrangement of the illumination sources changes. The system reduces the need for manual recalibration or reprogramming after luminaires are moved, reoriented, added, removed, or replaced. By basing control on detected source locations and, when available, source orientation or luminaire characteristics, the controller can dynamically adapt the lighting commands so that the intended illumination effect remains aligned with the independently defined reference point or scene location. This enables flexible, robust rendering of lighting scenes in environments such as homes, offices, studios, theaters, retail spaces, exhibition areas, hospitality venues, or other spaces in which lighting effects are expected to remain consistent despite changes in the lighting installation.
outputs.L5:
A lighting system is an important part of any building, home, or outdoor space. It provides visibility, improves safety, and helps create a comfortable atmosphere. A good lighting system is designed to meet the needs of the people using the space while also saving energy.

There are different types of lighting used in a lighting system. General lighting provides overall brightness for a room or area. Task lighting is used for specific activities, such as reading, cooking, or working at a desk. Accent lighting highlights special features, such as artwork, plants, or architectural details.

Modern lighting systems often use LED lights because they are energy-efficient, long-lasting, and available in many colors and brightness levels. Some systems also include smart controls, allowing users to adjust the lights with a remote control, smartphone, or voice command. Timers, motion sensors, and dimmers can also help reduce electricity use.

A well-designed lighting system can make a space more functional and attractive. In homes, it can create a warm and welcoming environment. In offices, it can improve concentration and productivity. In public areas, it can increase safety and security. Overall, a lighting system plays a key role in both the appearance and performance of any space.

counterfactuals.output:
Below is example claim language for a lighting control system. This is drafting language only and should be reviewed/adapted by patent counsel for the specific disclosure and jurisdiction.

## Example Independent System Claim

1. **A lighting control system**, comprising:  
   a plurality of luminaires, each luminaire comprising:  
   a light source;  
   a communication interface; and  
   one or more sensors configured to generate luminaire characteristic data indicative of at least one of a position, an orientation, or a luminaire type of the luminaire; and  

   a controller communicatively coupled to the plurality of luminaires and configured to:  
   receive the luminaire characteristic data from the plurality of luminaires;  
   determine, based at least in part on the received luminaire characteristic data, a spatial and/or functional arrangement of the plurality of luminaires;  
   associate one or more of the plurality of luminaires with a lighting scene based on the determined spatial and/or functional arrangement; and  
   generate adapted lighting scene control signals for the associated one or more luminaires, wherein the adapted lighting scene control signals are modified according to the detected position, orientation, and/or luminaire type of the associated one or more luminaires.

## Example Independent Method Claim

2. **A method of controlling a lighting system comprising a plurality of luminaires**, the method comprising:  
   detecting, by one or more sensors of respective luminaires, luminaire characteristic data indicative of at least one of a position, an orientation, or a luminaire type of the respective luminaires;  
   communicating the luminaire characteristic data to a controller;  
   determining, by the controller and based at least in part on the luminaire characteristic data, a spatial and/or functional arrangement of the plurality of luminaires;  
   selecting or modifying a lighting scene based on the determined spatial and/or functional arrangement; and  
   transmitting, by the controller, adapted lighting scene control signals to one or more of the plurality of luminaires, the adapted lighting scene control signals being configured to cause the one or more luminaires to emit light according to the selected or modified lighting scene and according to the detected position, orientation, and/or luminaire type of the one or more luminaires.

## Example Independent Controller Claim

3. **A controller for a lighting control system including a plurality of luminaires**, the controller comprising:  
   one or more processors; and  
   memory storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the controller to:  
   receive, from the plurality of luminaires, sensor-derived data indicative of at least one of position, orientation, or luminaire type;  
   determine relative placement and/or operating capability of the plurality of luminaires based on the sensor-derived data;  
   map a lighting scene to the plurality of luminaires based on the determined relative placement and/or operating capability; and  
   output lighting scene control signals that are adapted for individual luminaires based on the respective detected position, orientation, and/or luminaire type of the individual luminaires.

## Example Dependent Claims

4. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the one or more sensors comprise at least one of an accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, camera, depth sensor, proximity sensor, optical sensor, RFID reader, barcode reader, wireless ranging sensor, ultra-wideband sensor, Bluetooth direction-finding sensor, or near-field communication sensor.

5. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the luminaire characteristic data comprises orientation data indicating an aiming direction, tilt angle, pan angle, mounting angle, or beam direction of a luminaire.

6. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the luminaire characteristic data comprises position data indicating an absolute position, relative position, room location, zone location, or distance from another luminaire or reference device.

7. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the luminaire characteristic data comprises luminaire type data indicating at least one of a downlight, spotlight, wall-washer, cove light, pendant light, linear luminaire, color-capable luminaire, tunable-white luminaire, dimmable luminaire, beam-angle capability, lumen output capability, or color gamut capability.

8. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to automatically assign the plurality of luminaires to one or more lighting zones based on the received luminaire characteristic data.

9. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to adapt the lighting scene control signals by changing at least one of intensity, color, color temperature, beam direction, beam width, fade time, activation timing, or luminaire grouping.

10. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to compensate for an orientation of a luminaire by modifying a light output parameter associated with the luminaire.

11. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to compensate for a detected luminaire type by selecting only control parameters supported by the detected luminaire type.

12. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to adapt a stored lighting scene after detecting that one or more luminaires have been moved, rotated, replaced, added, or removed.

13. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to compare the detected position, orientation, and/or luminaire type of a luminaire with expected configuration data and to generate a notification when a mismatch is detected.

14. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to create a lighting scene map correlating physical locations of the plurality of luminaires with corresponding scene control parameters.

15. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the adapted lighting scene control signals comprise digital lighting control commands transmitted using at least one of DALI, DMX, Zigbee, Bluetooth Mesh, Wi-Fi, Thread, Ethernet, Power over Ethernet, or a proprietary lighting control protocol.

16. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein at least one luminaire includes an onboard processor configured to process raw sensor measurements to generate the luminaire characteristic data before transmission to the controller.

17. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to infer the luminaire type based on sensor-detected identifying information associated with a luminaire housing, optical element, driver, module, tag, or connector.

18. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to adapt the lighting scene control signals to maintain a desired illumination distribution despite a change in position or orientation of at least one luminaire.

19. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to perform commissioning of the lighting control system automatically based on the luminaire characteristic data.

20. The lighting control system of claim 1, wherein the adapted lighting scene control signals are individualized for respective luminaires such that two luminaires associated with a common lighting scene receive different control parameters based on their respective detected positions, orientations, and/or luminaire types.
